content.title: About
content.content: Olive tapenade is a spread made from finely chopped olives, often combined with capers, anchovies, garlic, olive oil, and seasonings. It has a rich, slightly salty and aromatic flavor typical of Mediterranean cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the French word “tapenade,” originally meaning a paste made from capers.
Traditional tapenade is made with black olives, though green‑olive versions are common.
Classic recipes frequently include anchovies, which add depth to the flavor.
Tapenade is usually served as an appetizer with bread, crackers, or vegetable sticks.
There are many regional variations, adding ingredients such as tomatoes, nuts, or fresh herbs.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Olives contain polyphenols like oleuropein that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Olive oil in tapenade is high in oleic acid, which supports heart health.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E supports immune function and protects cells from damage.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Capers and garlic provide dietary fiber and compounds that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Tapenade contains virtually no sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Allergy to olives or anchovies
items.content: People allergic to olives, fish, or shellfish may experience reactions.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Tapenade is often salty; individuals with hypertension should limit portion size.

items.title: Capers can be very acidic
items.content: Those with acid‑sensitive stomachs may experience discomfort from large amounts of capers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tapenade as a dip with baguette slices, crackers, or vegetable sticks, or use it as a spread for sandwiches and burgers. It can also be stirred into pasta, added to salads, or used as a sauce for fish and meat.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep tapenade in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. For longer storage, freeze in small portions; thaw in the fridge before use.
